$description: App experience density. Remapped under [data-experience=app] in generated web.css.

typography.$description:
The App's own chrome type scale (#1073). The Web group's four roles are the shared vocabulary; this group is the App's *density* for them plus the two levels a phone needs and a desktop does not. The values are deliberately not refs to `experience.web.typography`: a phone is held closer and read at arm's length in short bursts, and the Web scale (12.5/11/10/12) is a desktop density that reached the App by inheritance rather than by decision — `experience.web.typography` is emitted at `:root`, so every shared shell/workspace variable the App consumed resolved to Web's numbers (#1073 "Current mobile type inventory"). The two groups therefore share *roles* while each states its own size, which is the model `visual-language.md` already states for Experience tokens generally. A role still owns SIZE only — family and weight stay orthogonal, so a mono path is a path at the path's size rather than a smaller string. Work surfaces are out of scope by construction: xterm reads `experience.app.terminal` and CodeMirror reads `workspace.editorFontSize`, and neither is a chrome role.

The settled ramp is 17 / 16 / 14 / 13 / 12 / 13. Each value was chosen by looking at the canonical App screens at 375x812 and 390x844 (`/#/fixture/app`) and is recorded on the role it belongs to; the ramp #1073 proposed is a range and two of its values moved once a screen was in front of them. `title` and `body` are the two roles Web has no leaf for, so they are emitted only under `[data-experience="app"]`; a binding that consumes them must say which experience it belongs to (`nession/no-cross-experience-token`), which is what `web/src/app/experiences/app/appTypography.ts` exists to do.

title.$description: The page's own name: the active Session in the App header, the Workspace capability in its tool header, and a pushed detail's title. Settled at 17 by looking at the canonical App screens, not from the ramp in #1073: at the inherited `text-base` (16px) the title was the *same* size as the capsule's text field on the Terminal screen, so the page's name and the box the user types into were indistinguishable in the one place the title has the screen to itself; 17 restores a step. One step rather than several, because the title shares a 390px column with the rows below it — a 20px title would buy the page nothing and cost the Session list a line.

primary.$description: Work / navigation primary — the row the surface exists for: a Session name, a file name. Settled at 16 by looking: the App's own search field is pinned at 16px, because a smaller font in a focused input makes iOS Safari zoom the page and that is a platform behaviour this scale cannot design around. Web's 12.5px therefore did not just make the rows small, it made the field that *filters* the list 28% larger than the list — the inversion #1073 records as "the search field visually dominates the Session names". A primary role below the input floor reproduces that no matter how it is tuned, so the role sits at the floor instead: the content is never out-ranked by the control that acts on it. Verified at 375 and 390 that six Session rows and the chrome above them still fit without scrolling.

body.$description: Controls and ordinary actions: New Session, Filters, the status chips, the sort row, the file-viewer's Edit/Save/View actions. A control's size follows its *job*, not the primitive it happens to be built from, and the App rendered every one of these at `Button size="sm"`'s `text-xs` (12px) — smaller than the search placeholder above them and smaller than the metadata under the rows they act on, which is fine print. 14 rather than 15: at 15 a control and a Session row are within a pixel and the actions start reading as content, which is the axis the two roles exist to keep apart. Web keeps its 12px: a pointer has no reading-distance problem and the same `Button size="sm"` is correct there.

secondary.$description: Supporting but fully readable: a node row under a section label, and the tree/list text on the Files surface. Distinct from `primary` because the App demotes infrastructure context — the Agents disclosure is one muted row until asked for, and its rows must not read as work items (the same decision `SessionList` records for filing Sessions flat). Settled at 13 by looking at the disclosure open at 375: node rows at the inherited 11.5px were the same size as the "Agents" label above them, so a section and its rows read as one list instead of two levels.

metadata.$description: Quiet: agent/location, recency, counts, section labels, the footer's service state, the file-list metadata line. Settled at 12 by looking, and 12 is a floor rather than a preference: at Web's 10px the Session row's `codex · devbox-01 · 24d ago` was the hardest line on the Sessions screen to read at 375, and it is the line that tells two similarly-named Sessions apart — "metadata never outweighs the thing it describes" is a relationship between the two, not a licence to drop below what a phone can read at arm's length.

code.$description: Chrome-side technical identity: the path above the tree, and the file header above the editor (the pushed detail's own title is the `title` role, also in mono). Mono does not imply smaller — the family says "this is a path", the size says "this is a header", and the two are independent (#1073 criterion 6). Settled at 13 by looking at the pushed file detail at 375: the viewer's path header at Web's 11.5px was smaller than the file-list metadata on the screen it was pushed from, so the header naming the open file was the quietest text about it. Not the code surface itself: CodeMirror and xterm keep their own metrics, and on the App the pushed detail's code stays at CodeMirror's 12px.

control.$description: sm == md on purpose: app has a touch-target floor (touchTarget.min, 44px), so no control *hit target* may sit below it. Web keeps a real 28/32/36 scale because a pointer has no minimum hit area. Do not 'restore' a smaller app sm — that reintroduces sub-44px tap targets. `visualSize` is the one legitimate sub-44px dimension in this group and the only exception to the floor: it is not a hit target, it is the affordance painted *inside* one (#1034), so it must stay strictly below `md`.

visualSize.$description: The affordance actually painted inside a control — the circle a capsule icon action draws — as opposed to the box that receives the tap. A control keeps its `control.md` hit target (44px) and draws this smaller circle inside it (#1034), so a row of secondary actions stops reading as a row of primary buttons. The inequality is the point: 36 < 44 on App, and a value that reached or passed the hit target would be the silent revert the design gate fails. Declared in both experiences because one class serves both — an App-only leaf would resolve to nothing at `:root`.

shell.$description: App overrides for the shared sidebar tokens. Until #1073 this group held only geometry, so every text leaf under `experience.web.shell` was emitted at `:root` and inherited unchanged: the App rendered Session names, section labels, node rows and its footer at Web's desktop densities. `Sidebar`, `SessionItem`, `SidebarSectionHead`, `SidebarAgents` and `SidebarFooter` are one implementation serving both experiences, so the difference has to live in the token rather than in a branch — which is why these are remaps of the same leaf names and not new App-only ones.

sessionRowTitleFontSize.$description: Session name — the primary role. Same leaf, same role, the App's density.

sessionRowMetaFontSize.$description: Session metadata (agent / recency / the workload hint) — the metadata role. The role owns size, so the mono workload slot and the two product-text slots share this value; family is decided per slot, not here.

nodeFontSize.$description: Agent/node row text — the secondary role on App. Web states 11.5px here as a size of its own because Web's Agents section is a fixed part of its column; the App demotes Agents to a collapsed disclosure (#1050 stage 3), where a node row is supporting context under a label and must stay visibly quieter than a Session name without dropping to the metadata floor. Deriving it from `secondary` says that; the value it resolves to is 13px, not Web's 11.5px.

sectionHeadFontSize.$description: Sidebar section label on App — the metadata role. Quieter than the rows it names, which is the rule (`visual-language.md`); on App it also has to stay a step under the controls that sit in the same column.

footFontSize.$description: Sidebar foot text — the metadata role. A service state and a node count: quiet, and still readable on a phone.

sessionsListMinHeight.$description: How much of the App Sessions surface the Session list keeps for itself, as a share of that surface. The surface is a column of chrome above the list and a status foot below it, and at a short viewport (a phone held in landscape, #1057) the chrome alone can be taller than the surface — the column it replaced measured 328px of chrome at 390px tall, which left the list wrapper at exactly 0px and every Session row unreachable. A share rather than a pixel floor: the surface is 390px on one phone and 932px on another, and a length tuned to either would be wrong on the other. The chrome yields first and scrolls inside what is left, so the list holds this floor without the surface overflowing. It is deliberately not binding at the canonical portrait viewports, where the list already measures ~68% of the surface — it is the crisis floor for a short one.

terminal.$description: The App work surface's own typography and inset — the counterpart of `experience.web.terminal`, so the same leaf names exist on both sides and neither resolves to nothing outside its own experience. The mockup's `.phone-term` draws `font-size: 11.5px; line-height: 1.7; padding: 14px 14px 96px`: a step smaller and a step looser than Web, because the App terminal is read at arm's length on a smaller surface. The 96px bottom is the App capsule's box plus safe area and is therefore measured (`--terminal-content-bottom-inset`), not frozen here — see the same note in `experience/web.json`.

lineHeight.$description: Converted, not transcribed — same unit difference as `experience.web.terminal.lineHeight`, same method. The mockup's `.phone-term` CSS `line-height: 1.7` multiplies the font size: 11.5px × 1.7 = a 19.55px line box. xterm multiplies the font's measured box instead, 1.30em = 14.95px at 11.5px. The number that reproduces the mockup's leading is therefore 19.55 ÷ 14.95 = 1.31; the mockup's raw `1.7` would draw a 25px row, 28% looser.

projectionMarginBottom.$description: Gap between an emerged projection and the capsule below it. Close enough to read as attached to it, far enough that the two surfaces do not merge.

projectionMaxHeight.$description: Ceiling for an emerged projection (#826 Q5). Lower than Web's: the App capsule sits closer to the bottom edge and its projection has less room above it for the same content.

projectionFontSize.$description: One step below the capsule's own scale. A Signal is the smallest identifying state, not the composer's text, so it must not arrive at the field's size.

projectionMarkWidth.$description: The change letter's column (M/A/D/?) in a compact listing. Fixed so the filenames beside it share a left edge.

dockTarget.$description: App dock targets: the workspace-navigation band declares touchTarget.compact (#730) instead of the 44px chrome floor, because it floats over the terminal rather than taking a row from it. control-md is 44px on app by design, so this cannot borrow it.

workspace.$description: App overrides for the Workspace surface's chrome text. The App does not reuse the Web layout — `FilesAppLayout` pushes the tree full-screen and then the viewer over it — but it composes the same `FileList` / `FileViewer`, so the leaves that carry text are the same ones Web states. Only the chrome is remapped: the code surface itself (`workspace.editorFontSize`, read by CodeMirror) and Markdown document typography stay on Web's values, because they are the workload's own rendering and not chrome (#1073 non-goals).

treeFontSize.$description: Tree/list text — the secondary role, as on Web. Mono, because a path is technical identity; the role owns the size, not the family.

listRowTitleFontSize.$description: The file/directory row's name — the primary role, which is the row's work item on the Files surface. Declared here rather than left to the `text-sm` literal `FileList` used to carry: that literal was a Tailwind primitive default doing a product role's job, and it was the last size on the Files screen with no owner.

editorHeadFontSize.$description: The file path above the code — the code role. It names what is open by naming a path, so it is technical identity in chrome rather than a title competing with the work (which is why it is not `title`), and it is not metadata either: on a phone it is the only thing telling the user which file they are in.

editorActionFontSize.$description: The viewer's own controls (Edit / Save / View / Raw / close). The body role, like every other App control — the shared `Button size="sm"` default (`text-xs`) is a desktop density that the App inherited, and it left the file detail's actions as the smallest text on the screen they act on.
